messages.subject: Re: Packrat cannot install BH 1.55.0-3 through RStudio
messages.subject_clean: Packrat cannot install BH 1.55.0-3 through RStudio
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simeon,

This is an issue with packrat + the latest release of R (3.2.0) on OS X. In short, the default 'pkgType' option has changed to 'both', which the CRAN release of packrat unfortunately does not understand (and so constructs incorrect URLs when attempting to download package sources).

There are currently two workarounds:

1. Set `options(pkgType = "mac.binary.mavericks")` in your R session before running the associated packrat commands (and consider putting this into the project .Rprofile),
2. Install the latest version of packrat on GitHub (packrat::install_github('rstudio/packrat') and use that instead, as it should have a fixfor this issue.

We plan to submit a new version of packrat to CRAN within the next couple months and so this issue should be resolved then.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject_clean: Using Packrat with Travis-CI and AppVeyor
messages.body_plain:
Can someone point me towards a working example where packrat <https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/> is used with AppVeyor <https://ci.appveyor.com/> or Travis-CI to build an R package? Searching through Google and GitHub, I can't find any packrat-enable package that uses AppVeyor.  For Travis, I've found a few examples <https://github.com/richfitz/wood/blob/master/.travis.yml> that use @craig-citro 's initial r-travis <https://github.com/craigcitro/r-travis> approach, but I'd like to start this package with the newer approach of native R support <http://docs.travis-ci.com/user/languages/r/>.

Do the yaml files need to change? Are there some settings I need to add through the Travis/AppVeyor websites?  I have a very minimal package (testthat is the only dependency) that broke Travis & AppVeyor builds. Here is the code frozen for that commit <https://github.com/OuhscBbmc/Premiss/tree/f110944be3e1b02d53ffbe69b71fc5d2d9dd6615>. Here is the Travis-CI log <https://travis-ci.org/OuhscBbmc/Premiss/builds/60886183>; here is the AppVeyor log <https://ci.appveyor.com/project/wibeasley/premiss/build/1.0.10>.
Since RStudio developers created Packrat, and advocate GitHub and CI, I thought I could find more examples of the two components working together in the same Package.

Two weeks ago I posted these questions separately in StackOverflow without much response.  I earned a StackOverflow tumbleweed <http://stackoverflow.com/help/badges/63/tumbleweed> badge.
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/29997095/building-r-packages-with-packrat-and-travis-ci
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/29996468/building-r-packages-with-packrat-and-appveyor
Thanks, Will

messages.body_plain:
That weird error is a consequence of the old layout of the packrat cache. You'll have to manually remove these packages (that is, their symlinks) with:

    file.remove(file.path(packrat:::libDir(), "packrat"))

After that, you should be able to re-install packrat.

Kevin

messages.subject: Re: Problem when creating a package
messages.body_plain:
I am not sure which direction you are going with this, but our current approach to deployment is to copy over the entire packrat/lib onto the production server. Since most of our production applications are basically back ends to a shiny app, the only thing we had to do to make this work is have the shiny app add the correct project to libPaths before doing anything else.

This setup is a little trickier for non-shiny R sessions. We have a utility that the user calls in lieu of 'library' which adds the project library to libPaths and then loads the library. This has been adequate for us since only devs are using R sessions.

So, for us the desirable default behavior is to build the package into the packrat library and nowhere else.

Cheers,
Yasmin

> Good point -- it isn't immediately obvious, but I think one would want to install it into the private Packrat library, and then load it from there -- ie, if package development is going to live in the Packrat library, then we should ensure it's installed and used there.

> On the flip side, we need some mechanism for telling Packrat that a package is ready to be 'released into the wild', since obviously the net result is a package that we want in the user library. Perhaps it should be installed into both places by default, even?

> I think the tricky bit is differentiating between when we are:

messages.subject: Avoid re-installing packages that have been installed
messages.subject_clean: Avoid re-installing packages that have been installed
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Sometimes I feel it is unnecessary and time-consuming to re-install a
package of a certain version that has been installed in the system or
user's library. For example, I really hate reinstalling packages like
XML/RCurl/stringi/... from source on Linux:
https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets/blob/gh-pages/packrat/packrat.lock
I wonder if it is possible for packrat to avoid installing such
packages if their required versions have already been installed, e.g.
I have installed XML 3.98-1.1 (via apt-get install r-cran-xml), and I
wish packrat could just use it, instead of downloading the source from
CRAN and compiling it from source.

In other words, I wish packrat is more about package versions than
rebuilding the whole universe unconditionally :)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Avoid re-installing packages that have been installed
messages.subject_clean: Avoid re-installing packages that have been installed
messages.body_plain:
One thing that packrat has that attempts to make this possible is the 'external.packages' project option. The idea is that, for all packages listed in 'external.packages', packrat will attempt to load those from the user library rather than the local packrat library.

You could try e.g.

    packrat::opts$external.packages(c("XML", "RCurl", "stringi"))

Either way, this issue hallmarks some of the tension with packrat as a tool for reproducible project management, and a tool simply for package management (with less emphasis on reproducible).

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Kevin. It seems opts$external.packages can solve this
particular problem, but it may violate principles of reproducibility,
since there is no guarantee the versions of external packages are what
was specified in the packrat.lock file (or there is?). At the moment,
I don't mind reinstalling a package if the project author requires a
different version in the lock file. It is just that I don't want to
reinstall the same version. I guess there is a lot of redundancy by
reinstalling everything, and we don't necessarily lose reproducibility
by using some packages from the system's global R package libraries as
long as the version requirement is satisfied.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject_clean: Avoid re-installing packages that have been installed
messages.body_plain:
If the version of X in the global library has changed, I'm fine with
reinstalling the desired version specified in packrat.lock.

Personally I don't like locking down versions. I tend to continuously
test new versions as soon as they become available, and upgrade if I
don't find problems. I understand this sounds risky and is a bad idea
in certain cases. I think there are two approaches to reproducibility:
locking down the environment, or testing as we move forward. I cannot
tell which is uniformly better (both have pros and cons), but usually
my own preference is the latter.

Regards,
Yihui
